body:
hi there -

have you set NLS_LANG correctly?      since you're running a straight string SQL statement, this is a basic cx_Oracle issue.       Need to know what NLS_LANG is set to.

@zzzeek 
NLS_LANG is correctly.
`os.environ['NLS_LANG'] = 'SIMPLIFIED CHINESE_CHINA.UTF8'`

under the "=====================" is output from cx_Oracle

there's not much I can do here as this is a basic round trip, can you please try the cx_Oracle DBAPI directly and report it over at https://github.com/oracle/python-cx_Oracle/issues

```


import cx_Oracle

connection = cx_Oracle.connect(...)   # see https://cx-oracle.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/connection_handling.html#establishing-database-connections

cursor = connection.cursor()
cursor.execute("SELECT <your statement>")
cursor.description
```

unless you are talking about the difference between result.keys() and saved_cursor.description ?    I can't really see your screenshot.   I would need a test case and at least give me those chinese characters to work with.   also python 2 vs. python 3 info is needed

@zzzeek this is my code and result.

from sqlalchemy import create_engine, event
import cx_Oracle
import os

os.environ['NLS_LANG'] = 'SIMPLIFIED CHINESE_CHINA.UTF8'

sqlString = "select  姓名, 姓名 as 姓名id from 病人信息"


"""
use sqlalchemy
"""
engine = create_engine("oracle+cx_oracle://*********************")
conn = engine.connect()
cursor = conn.execute(sqlString)
print("sqlalchemy: {0}".format(cursor.keys()))

print("========================== split ==================================")


"""
use cx_oracle
"""
conn = cx_Oracle.connect("***************")
cursor = conn.cursor()
cursor.execute(sqlString)
print("cx_oracle: {0}".format([i[0] for i in cursor.description]))

![Snipaste_2019-10-23_21-31-31](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9586655/67397958-8edd7880-f5dc-11e9-94ba-b899637f00de.png)

rename.from: chinese column name garbled in oracle
rename.to: oracle name normalize fails for international characters

body: name_normalize converts from oracle's UPPERCASE as case-insensitive to SQLAlchemy's lower case as case-insensitive and it does not expect characters for which "upper" / "lower" make no sense to be part of this.  for some reason name normalize is running on this.

rename.from: oracle name normalize fails for international characters

body:
okey doke this is not as broken as it seemed.   the repr() for quoted name is confusing because it is using a py2k-style repr.

(Pdb) cursor.keys()[0] == cursor._saved_cursor.description[0][0]
True

the two names you see are the same string, just different representations:
```

Python 3.7.4 (default, Jul  9 2019, 16:32:37) 
[GCC 9.1.1 20190503 (Red Hat 9.1.1-1)] on linux
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> x = '\u59d3\u540d'
>>> y = '姓名'
>>> x == y
True

```


will see if we can use default `__repr__` under python 3.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Use default repr() for quoted_name under python 3** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1537

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **rel_1_3** branch:

**Use default repr() for quoted_name under python 3** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1538
